transcript.text: Hannah, Liam, your tourism project compares four small destinations. Hannah, start with Lake Town.
transcript.speaker: DR OKAFOR

transcript.text: We chose them because they are all very different, so the comparison should show some interesting patterns.
transcript.speaker: LIAM

transcript.text: Good. Make sure you explain that choice in the introduction.
transcript.speaker: DR OKAFOR

transcript.text: Lake Town is beautiful, but in summer it's overcrowded. The one main street has coaches parked all along it.
transcript.speaker: HANNAH

transcript.text: Old Port is the opposite. It's quiet, but there's no direct train, so you need two buses and a very long wait.
transcript.speaker: LIAM

transcript.text: The Mountain Village has far fewer visitors than it could cope with, but not enough beds. Most hotels have just ten rooms.
transcript.speaker: HANNAH

transcript.text: And the Desert Camp is expensive. A night costs more than a flight to the capital.
transcript.speaker: LIAM

transcript.text: The Desert Camp also offers special evening activities, so some visitors think it is worth the money.
transcript.speaker: HANNAH

transcript.text: That's a good counter-argument. Will you include the visitors' opinions as well?
transcript.speaker: DR OKAFOR

transcript.text: Interesting. Did weather come up?
transcript.speaker: DR OKAFOR

transcript.text: Only for the desert, but that's why it's open in winter only. We didn't count it as a problem.
transcript.speaker: HANNAH

transcript.text: Right. Let's move on to the practical side of the project.
transcript.speaker: DR OKAFOR

transcript.text: For the fieldwork, how will you collect data?
transcript.speaker: DR OKAFOR

transcript.text: We'll use a questionnaire in three languages, which we'll hand out at the tourist office.
transcript.speaker: LIAM

transcript.text: That is ambitious. Which languages have you chosen?
transcript.speaker: DR OKAFOR

transcript.text: English, Spanish and German, because those are the most common among tourists there.
transcript.speaker: LIAM

transcript.text: We also want to interview local business owners, particularly guesthouse owners, because they know about seasonal changes.
transcript.speaker: HANNAH

transcript.text: We've already had the questionnaire checked by a friend who studies languages, so the translations should be accurate.
transcript.speaker: LIAM

transcript.text: Good. A pilot test with a few people would be wise too.
transcript.speaker: DR OKAFOR

transcript.text: Be careful with timing. When do you plan to travel?
transcript.speaker: DR OKAFOR

transcript.text: The second week of June, before the summer rush. We'll stay four nights in each place.
transcript.speaker: LIAM

transcript.text: We'll keep a diary every evening to record our own impressions as well.
transcript.speaker: HANNAH

transcript.text: Excellent. Researchers' notes can be a really valuable source of data.
transcript.speaker: DR OKAFOR

transcript.text: What will be your biggest challenge, do you think?
transcript.speaker: DR OKAFOR

transcript.text: Probably the budget. The department gives us four hundred pounds, but transport alone will cost more.
transcript.speaker: HANNAH

transcript.text: Have you thought about applying for the travel grant? The deadline is the end of this month.
transcript.speaker: DR OKAFOR

transcript.text: We didn't know about it. Where do we apply?
transcript.speaker: LIAM

transcript.text: On the student services page. You'll need a letter from me, so email me today.
transcript.speaker: DR OKAFOR

transcript.text: Will do. And if we don't get it?
transcript.speaker: HANNAH

transcript.text: Then drop the Desert Camp. It's the most expensive, and the other three give you enough material.
transcript.speaker: DR OKAFOR

transcript.text: That's helpful, thank you. We'll start the application this afternoon.
transcript.speaker: HANNAH

transcript.text: Good luck with it. Let me know how you get on.
transcript.speaker: DR OKAFOR
